primary.title: Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung
primary.author: Mao Zedong
primary.rationale: This is a collection of Mao's writings and speeches, widely disseminated and a key text for understanding his ideology and the Cultural Revolution. It is highly likely to be found in digital archives.

primary.title: On Practice
primary.author: Mao Zedong
primary.rationale: A foundational philosophical essay by Mao, outlining his theory of knowledge and dialectical materialism. Important for understanding his intellectual development.

primary.title: On Contradiction
primary.author: Mao Zedong
primary.rationale: Another key philosophical work by Mao, elaborating on the concept of contradiction as the driving force of change. Essential for understanding his dialectical thinking.

secondary.title: Mao: The Unknown Story
secondary.author: Jung Chang and Jon Halliday
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and controversial biography that offers a critical perspective on Mao's life and rule, based on extensive research.

secondary.title: Mao Zedong and China in the Twentieth-Century World: A Concise History
secondary.author: Rebecca E. Karl
secondary.rationale: A scholarly overview that places Mao's life and leadership within the broader context of 20th-century global history, offering a balanced academic assessment.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Mao Zedong
secondary.author: Rebecca E. Karl and Laura J. Song (Editors)
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars providing diverse perspectives on Mao's thought, actions, and legacy.

suggestions.notes: Primary source texts by Mao are often available in collections of his works or as standalone essays on platforms like Internet Archive and Wikisource. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and publication date post-Mao's death.
